candidates.title: [autocomplete] regression in behavior for freeSolo Autocomplete with custom Popper/Paper and no options
candidates.reason: Source-qualified unsplit fixture with original content/timeout criterion; final independent checks pending.
candidates.issueBody:
### Steps to reproduce Old behavior: https://stackblitz.com/edit/react-ouzbqw-wbhjow?file=Demo.tsx,package.json New behavior: https://stackblitz.com/edit/react-ouzbqw-vpfhhc?file=Demo.tsx,package.json' Steps: 1) Open autocomplete and wait 3 seconds for options to be set to `[]` 2) click `SET DEFAULT OPTIONS` to reset and try again ### Current behavior When options prop is set to `[]` the Autocomplete Popper is no longer rendered. The Autocomplete's state still considers itself open and the onClose handler is not called. Any custom Popper/Paper used in the Autocomplete will not be rendered. ### Expected behavior The Autocomplete stays open if you have a custom Popper/Paper so that you can display other information or maybe even a custom "No Items" option. ### Context In our case we have a custom Autocomplete used as a global site search that renders a custom Popper/Paper that includes chips that link to certain "Advanced search" options as well as contains a recently searched section (the Autocomplete's options) that will show recent results. In our current version of MUI v5.10.17 when there are no recent search options the Autocomplete can still be expanded and the Chips used to navigate to advanced search pages. ![capture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c76f0022-a612-4cc7-9c63-dff101559669) ![capture2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/354d461e-8639-4527-a926-4498257dac54) However, updating to the latest 5.x version of MUI v5.16.7 (bug also present in latest 6.x version) when there are no recent search options and the Autocomplete's options prop is `[]` it will not open, or it will close the Autocomplete if the user has expanded it and options is asynchronously loaded and results in an empty data result. Also when the Autocomplete closes asynchronously because of `options=[]` it will not call onClose or update its internal `open` state unless the user does an action that makes it realize it is no longer open (such as clicking somewhere and causing a blur event). This regression was introduced in https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/41300 ### Your environment
npx @mui/envinfo ``` Don't forget to mention which browser you used. Output from `npx @mui/envinfo` goes here. ```
**Search keywords**: autocomplete freesolo no options custom popper paper

comments.body: It's a regression, as you mentioned, but we shouldn't revert #41300 since it fixes #40843. I haven't found a solution yet—any ideas?

i'm not sure what the best solution is, currently we are applying a patch to our internal application to go back to the old behavior

[@mui__material@5.16.7.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17561573/%40mui__material%405.16.7.patch)

i'm not sure whether this re-introduces #40843 or not since we never experienced that bug to begin with
@snapwich I have created a pull request to fix it: #44266. Feel free to check it out.
Is there any chance this will be officially fixed or patched? Currently it is stopping us from updating MUI unless we put in a workaround ourselves.
I have reverted for v5 in #44857. It should be available in the next version 5 release. I'll close this issue.

**This issue has been closed.** If you have a similar problem but not exactly the same, please open a [new issue](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/new/choose).
Now, if you have additional information related to this issue or things that could help future readers, feel free to leave a comment.
> [!NOTE]
> @snapwich How did we do? Your experience with our support team matters to us. If you have a moment, please share your thoughts in this short [Support Satisfaction survey](https://tally.mui.com/support-satisfaction-survey?issue=44048&productId=material-ui).

candidates.title: Regression: Existing Sketch plugin icons are not modified when sync command is run
candidates.reason: Sketch plugin synchronization outside existing browser fixture context.
candidates.issueBody:
related #5758
related #5711

When running the icons sync command in the Sketch plugin, the existing artboards and symbols are not modified and the updated artwork is placed on new artboards instead. This is likely due to (breaking) name changes which were laying the groundwork for icon and pictogram plans for the plugin, but these plans may have shifted. We will need to confirm whether or not these plans are still on, and if not, we will investigate further into whether or not rolling back the name changes is a valid resolution for this issue. Resolving this issue will lead into resolving further issues detailed in #5749 and #6485

comments.body: Combination of #15897 and 578fd0bc. There doesn't seem to be any way to disable the active overlay now if I revert 578fd0bc.

I've been toying around with this one and the issue lies with the logic we use to determine if something has support for color. This change worked the best in all scenarios that I tested:

```ts
const hasColor = (
  (group?.isSelected.value && (!link.isLink.value || link.isActive?.value)) ||
  (!group && link.isActive?.value)
)
```

1. If an item is selected from a group and is not a link
2. If an item is selected from a group and is a link and is linkActive
3. If an item is not in a group and is linkActive

Tab sets active to false which removes the active state, but it still needs the ability to apply color from being selected in a group.  This worked before because hasColor wasn't influenced by the active state. 

It's worth noting that even with the above change, we don't have a way to have the group model change when the route changes from a currently active item that is also itself a router link.

This also might be a good candidate for an **active-variant** prop and get away from using the overlay/underlay stylistically.

candidates.title: [Bug Report] VCalendar regression in click handler when dealing with string categories
candidates.reason: Original mouse category event payload, not a keyboard task.
candidates.issueBody: ### Environment **Vuetify Version:** 2.4.2 **Last working version:** 2.3.23 **Vue Version:** 2.6.12 **Browsers:** Edge 87.0.664.66 **OS:** Windows 10 ### Steps to reproduce In v2.4, support for categories as objects was added. This seems to have introduced breaking changes to people who are using categories as an array of strings. Specifically, I use the @mousedown:time-category event handler. This handler is passed an event with a category field. That field is now a category object always. The reproduction link above creates a simple calendar with 2 categories that are simple strings cat 1 and cat 2. The handler receives the event and dumps it to the console. Note that when you click on the calendar, the event dumped to the console includes a category object with the name of the category in categoryName rather than category being a string as it used to be. This breaks all the code that used to process these events expecting the category to be a string. Also, the docs have not been updated to reflect that category can be an object now and not just a string. ### Expected Behavior the object dumped to the console should have shown category: 'cat 1' ### Actual Behavior the object dumped to the console now shows category as an object: { categoryName: 'cat 1' } ### Reproduction Link https://codepen.io/gregveres-the-looper/pen/BaLVvjK?editors=1111

candidates.issueBody:
The selector handling changes introduced in 3.3.0 break manual tooltips initialized with a selector.

http://jsfiddle.net/sk5o25b9/ (worked fine in 3.2.0)
http://jsfiddle.net/sk5o25b9/1 (busted in 3.3.0+)

See PR https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/pull/14189 and related commit https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/commit/1b3237629a316af41945e20837cf3a332798b264
Related to #14167

comments.body: I believe I have a fix for this: 465ef28
Nevermind...that seemed to have fixed it for tooltip selectors but broken it for tooltips without selectors. I'll see if I can find a more complete solution tomorrow.

I can't come up with a good, backwards-compatible way to fix this. I ran into this issue because I'm calling $().tooltip("destroy") where there is a selector, but @mattlunn's proposal would mean I would have to change my code to add the selector in there. It seems like it might be best to revert 1b32376 and look into a new way to handle selectors for v4.0 that fixes #14167.
Only thing I can think of would be to track the last selector given, and use that as the default for any future calls.

Maybe instead of storing the instance data per-selector, we could add an explicit `instanceId` (or whatever) option and store the data per-ID. And when no ID is provided, default to some special ID so that stuff not using `selector` still works.
Just a random thought.
@hnrch02 Any objection to reverting #14189 for the time being?
@cvrebert No, seems like this is a bigger issue than #14167. We'll see if we can address it in v4.

candidates.title: Regression in 1.6.5 – `clippingAncestors` not working on top layer elements
candidates.reason: Original visual layout/style or positioning criterion; no qualifying original keyboard failure established.
candidates.issueBody:
**Describe the bug** A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

`@floating-ui/dom` 1.6.5 introduced a regression on our library where collision detection doesn't work in relation to the ancestor. we managed to track it down to a specific change, introduced in #2887, which unintentionally has the counter effect of disabling `clippingAncestors` for any tooltip placed on the top layer element.

we use a `popover` attribute on the tooltip element (placing the tooltip on the top layer) to ensure the stacking context is consistent and correct across the library.

**To Reproduce**

WIP to reproduce in sandbox

Please use one of the following CodeSandboxes to reproduce your issue and make sure not to include any external libraries:

- @floating-ui/dom: https://codesandbox.io/s/floating-ui-dom-template-utpx0u

-->

**Expected behavior** A clear and concise description of what you expected to
happen.

The dropdown list should reposition when reaching one of the boundaries of the parent element.

**Context:**

- OS: [e.g. iOS]
- Browser [e.g. chrome, safari]
- Version [e.g. 22]

**Additional context** Add any other context about the problem here.

comments.body:
fwiw, the second link is private

This isn't a bug though. `clipping-ancestors` refers to ancestor elements that will visually clip the popover - for top-layer elements, they don't get clipped by containers (evidenced by the fact that you can see the popover overflow the container, and it's not clipped)

The correct way to fix this is to specify the scrolling container manually as the boundary if you want that behavior

I built multi-level menu using Bootstrap 4 popovers. It worked like a harm with Popper 1.12.6, but since 1.12.7 menu positioning is broken. Tested with all versions including 1.13.0-next.

Looks like the second-level popover is placed incorrectly. This is quite complicated code and I can't provide a simplified test case. Any hints on what changed in 1.12.7 that can cause this issue?

The popover is initialized using:
```
   .popover({
                content: content_element,
                trigger: 'manual',
                placement: 'right',
                animation: true,
                html: true
            })
```
Again, the element on which I create the new popover is already a child of opened popover.

comments.body:
I've found out that removing this in my stylesheet fixes the issue:
```
.popover-body { overflow-x: hidden; }
```
https://codepen.io/anon/pen/mpYmVX
So, it looks that if the button is inside of an element with `overflow-x:hidden` popover positioning is broken. I need scrolling in long menus, so I can't just remove it. Any remedy?
